## Recommendation
- **Go to St. Joseph first.** My estimate for boat salmon this week is about 3 of 4, with the caveat that its latest report is 20 days old.
- **South Haven or Muskegon as the backup**, each about 2 of 4.
- **Grand Haven is the weakest choice**, about 1 of 4, though its newest report (July 24) shows Chinook were being caught.
- **Fish 80-90 ft of water at St. Joseph** with spoons, and about 75-110 ft at South Haven with rotators and flies.
- **Run lines about 35-100 ft down**, which is where the recent boat reports caught fish.

## Why
- **St. Joseph has the best recent boat result:** the July 10 report rated Chinook and coho boat fishing excellent, with the best fish at 80-90 ft on spoons (St. Joseph, 2024-07-10).
- **Grand Haven ranks lowest because its newest boat ratings are weak:** the July 24 coho and unspecified-salmon boat reports were rated below average, and the Chinook report was not rated (Grand Haven, 2024-07-24).
- **I'd expect the St. Joseph result to hold only if the water stays cool:** that excellent week followed about 23 hours of north-to-east wind at 8+ mph, which likely pushed cold water in (St. Joseph, 2024-07-10).
- **Past years at similar water temperatures show boats doing well at 80-120 ft:** in late July and August 2023, boat anglers at these ports caught fish at 80-130 ft on spoons, meat rigs and flies (Grand Haven, 2023-08-09; St. Joseph, 2023-07-26).

## Evidence
**Recent reports**
- St. Joseph, 2024-07-10: Chinook and coho, boat, 80-90 ft, 80-90 ft down? The report gives the productive depth as 80-90 ft of water, spoons, quality 4 (excellent).
- South Haven, 2024-07-10: Chinook and coho, boat, 75-110 ft of water, best at 75-80 ft and 105-110 ft, rotators and flies, quality 2 (average).
- Muskegon, 2024-07-10: salmon, boat, 40-100 ft down in 70-120 ft of water, meat rigs and flashers, quality 2 (average).
- Grand Haven, 2024-07-24: Chinook boat fishing at 35-100 ft down in 60-120 ft of water, green and orange spoons and white flashers, not rated. Coho and unspecified salmon were rated 1 (below average).
- St. Joseph, 2024-07-03: only a few coho to boats, rated 1 (below average), best around 100 ft.

**Past seasons (similar surface temperature, my history lookup)**
- Grand Haven, 2023-08-09: good Chinook boat fishing at 50-100 ft down in 80-160 ft of water, plugs and meat rigs (quality 3).
- St. Joseph, 2023-07-26: good boat fishing around 120 ft on spoons (quality 3).
- Grand Haven, 2023-07-19 and 2022-07-14: boat fishing was mixed to slow in some years, with fish scattered across depths.

**Conditions now**
- Buoy surface water for the week before July 30 was about 73 F at St. Joseph, 71 F at South Haven, and 68 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon (buoy data, week before 2024-07-30). These are warmer than the 52-58 F range that Chinook prefer (NY DEC guidance), so the fish are likely deeper or near cooler water.
- Upwelling wind over the past 3 days was 0 hours at St. Joseph, 3 hours at South Haven, 2 hours at Grand Haven, and 5 hours at Muskegon (wind summary, week before 2024-07-30). I'd expect less cold water near the piers than during the July 10 week at St. Joseph.

## Caveats
- **The reports are old.** The newest reports are July 24 for Grand Haven and July 10 for the other three ports, so these are a guide rather than current conditions.
- **Live data was not available.** The conditions tool returned a summary of the week before July 30, with no wind forecast and no modeled cold-layer depth, so I couldn't check this weekend's wind or water.
- **The ratings are my estimates.** They come from one or two reports per port and are not a forecast.

## Sources
- St. Joseph, South Haven, Muskegon, Grand Haven (2024-07-10): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3a7bce5
- Grand Haven (2024-07-24): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3aa7f0e
